name: Trance-gate: sidechain-gate chop a sustained pad
goal: Turn a long sustaining pad/wall-of-sound (or heavily reverbed short source) into rhythmic stuttered chunks by sidechain-gating it from a silent trigger pattern (e.g. clustered 16ths), then tune gate release for snap and optionally re-space with post-gate reverb.

source.title: The trance gate technique (like Ross from Friends, Bicep, Max Cooper and Moderat)

prerequisites: DAW with sidechain-capable gate (or equivalent gain chop); sustained synth/pad source; optional muteable trigger track

inputs.name: source_patch
inputs.description: Long sustain / high sustain level (not a short pluck)

inputs.name: trigger_pattern
inputs.description: e.g. clusters of 3 sixteenth notes or every 16th

constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided Show-transcript text; do not invent UI paths or numeric settings not stated there.

Original synthesis / signal-flow only — map brand UI (Serum/Vital/Ableton/etc.) to portable osc/filter/env/LFO/FX modules for Traveler-inspired or Web Audio hybrid; never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Prefer transferable parameter relationships over vendor-specific preset or bank names.
Trigger track is for rhythm only—do not leave it audible in the final mix.
Map Ableton Gate sidechain UI to any host gate with external key input.

steps.action: Build a source that sustains loudly while held (long notes or short hits + lots of reverb/compression so the wash stays continuous). Optionally thicken with power-chord voicing (root + octave + perfect fifth / +7 st).
Create a separate trigger track with short clicks/samples on a 16th grid; classic patterns: repeating clusters of 3 sixteenths, or every 16th. Mute/do not mix the trigger into the output.
Put a gate on the source. Enable sidechain/external key from the trigger track. Raise/lower threshold until the source opens only when triggers fire.
Adjust gate release for more/less snap (shorter = choppier). Try alternate trigger densities.
Optional: same technique on a vocal snippet + huge reverb before the gate; add another reverb after the gate to reintroduce space around chops.

verification: Sustained source alone is continuous; with gate+trigger it chops in rhythm
Trigger track is silent in the mix
